//: Shared contract between the two halves of the password policy: api/src/password.rs and frontend/src/utils/passwordPolicy.ts. Both test suites read this file and must reach the same verdict for every vector, so a form can never accept what the API refuses, nor blame a different rule for the same password. Only the identity half is pinned here — the blocklist lives on the server alone. `verdict` is one of: acceptable, similarToEmail, similarToName.

vectors.why: The reported vulnerability: the password is the account's email address.
Decorating the address must not walk past the rule; the domain is public.
Lookalike substitutions must not hide the address.
A password that is mostly the user's name.
Ordinary first.last address whose halves are the user's names: both sides must blame the same rule. The two implementations used to disagree here, one saying email and the other name.
Astral characters: counted once as code points, twice as UTF-16 units. Counting units moved the remainder threshold and made the form accept what the API refuses.

Other_Alphabetic marks (Devanagari vowel sign): kept by Rust's is_alphanumeric, dropped by a naive \p{L}. Dropping them made the form refuse what the API accepts, for users writing in Indic, Thai, Arabic or Hebrew scripts.
A passphrase that merely contains a short name keeps its own strength.
A password that merely opens with the user name: the rest is still a secret.
A very short name must not reject unrelated passwords.
Folds to nothing: no identity to compare against. The length and diversity rules are what bound this one, on the server.

Folds to a single letter, which almost any address contains. Being inside the address only means something when there is enough of the password left to recognise; otherwise a pile of symbols gets blamed on the email.

//maximumLength: The password ceiling. Not operator-configurable, so the frontend mirrors the constant rather than fetching it; both suites check their own constant against this number, so the two cannot drift.
//rejectionProblemIds: Every API error that means 'the password was refused', as opposed to 'the request failed'. The API test suite checks this list against `Rejection::into_problem`, the frontend test suite checks it against the ids the forms attach to the password field: a rejection reason added on one side without the other stops being a silent toast-only error.
